newsitem.title: USA: EPA says unclear which areas will violate air rule.
newsitem.headline: EPA says unclear which areas will violate air rule.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency does not know how many counties will violate tough new limits it set for smog starting in 2004 and soot starting in 2005, an administration official said Tuesday.

"No one will know which counties will be in attainment or out of attainment, until we take new monitoring data," the official said. "Anyone claiming to have data on who's in or who's out is working on historical data."

His comments came in response to statements by House Commerce Committee leaders who have been pressing the EPA for estimates of how many counties that meet existing air quality rules will fall short of the new standards, in order to build support for a bill to postpone the rules.

The committee's top Republican and Democrat, Rep. Thomas Bliley of Virginia and Rep. John Dingell of Michigan have raised the specter that the strict standards will stifle investment, kill jobs, and trigger penalties, including a loss of federal highway funds, in cities that fail the standards.
EPA sent the committee estimates two weeks ago that 280 counties would violate smog-forming ozone rules and 150 would fail to meet fine particle standards.

But in a more recent report to the committee it revised the numbers based on 1993-1995 data, saying 546 counties would not meet the new smog standard and 283 would not meet the soot standard, out of about 3,200 counties nationwide.
"Get ready for hard times. Get ready for sanctions," Dingell said at a National Press Club luncheon Tuesday.
